```regex
^([01]\d|2[0-3]):[0-5]\d$
```

- `([01]\d|2[0-3])` matches hours 00–19 or 20–23. A plain `\d\d` would accept 24–99.
- `[0-5]\d` matches minutes 00–59.
- `^` and `$` anchor the match to the whole line, so surrounding text causes a non-match.

This requires two-digit hours, so `7:45` won't match. Use `^([01]?\d|2[0-3]):[0-5]\d$` if you want to accept single-digit hours.

For grep, use it with `-E` (extended syntax):

```bash
grep -E '^([01]\d|2[0-3]):[0-5]\d$' file.txt
```

Note that `\d` is not supported by all grep versions in extended mode. If yours rejects it, use `[0-9]` in place of each `\d`:

```regex
^([01][0-9]|2[0-3]):[0-5][0-9]$
```
